turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey, good to have you here. How are you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We booked bowling for my son's party. What do I need to sort beforehand?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nice choice. Have you checked if they do bumpers and lighter balls for kids?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I didn't think of that. They're nine.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask for bumpers, they make it more fun and less frustrating at that age. Also check how many kids per lane.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Different question. I'm taking a gap year after school and I've narrowed it down to a few plans.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm going to list all the options first, so please don't comment until I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Working at a ski lodge in Canada for the winter, then traveling with the money I've saved.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Volunteering on an organic farm in New Zealand, which gives me free food and a bed.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Teaching English in South Korea, with a proper salary but a one year contract.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Interrailing around Europe, which would be amazing, but I'd need to save for months first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, um, that's everything, I think. Your thoughts?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You could chain two of them, like the ski lodge for the winter and then interrailing with what you earn. The farm in New Zealand is good if you want calm. Korea is the most serious choice, best if you're curious about teaching.
